core_claim: For 16 consecutive years (2001-2016), no Best Picture winner has been the most-referenced film of its own year — the Academy and the culture have stopped agreeing on what counts.

edt_01.label: Hook — One year that contains the whole story (Spotlight 2015)
edt_01.title: Best Picture, Forgotten Picture
edt_01.editorial_notes: Open with the 358 vs 31 contrast (Force Awakens vs Spotlight). The 16-year drought (2001-2016) line is load-bearing — it must appear in this section.

edt_02.label: How we are measuring the culture (methodology + Casablanca anchor)
edt_02.title: What an IMDb 'connection' is
edt_02.editorial_notes: Explain crowdsourced movie-connections; flag recency problem; gesture to Bioglio/Pensa precedent. Casablanca's 48.7% gets a teaser mention here, full treatment in edt_06.

edt_03.label: Decade-by-decade collapse
edt_03.title: From 9% to 1.5%
edt_03.editorial_notes: The decade chart is the analytical centrepiece. 9.4% (1970s) and 1.5% (2010s) are exact numbers.

edt_04.label: Snubs that dwarf the prize (Empire Strikes Back vs Ordinary People)
edt_04.title: The 18.6x snub
edt_04.editorial_notes: Empire Strikes Back vs Ordinary People is the headline pair. 1980 ratio = 18.6x. 74 of 89 years (83%) is the cumulative line.

edt_05.label: The People's Best Pictures — the parallel canon
edt_05.title: The People's Best Pictures
edt_05.editorial_notes: Use the parallel-list framing. Reader should be able to scrub year-by-year and see the Academy pick vs the references pick.

edt_06.label: Peaks the Academy got right (Casablanca, Godfather, Rocky)
edt_06.title: When prize and culture aligned
edt_06.editorial_notes: Don't make this a victory lap — the function is to show what the alignment used to look like. Star Wars 1977 (4,965 references) is the all-time #1; mention it lost Best Picture to Annie Hall.

edt_07.label: Close — A different kind of Best Picture
edt_07.editorial_notes: End on the implication, not a summary. Avoid 'in conclusion'-style wrap-ups.
